subject: Post-call recap: environment selection and audit evidence scoping
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Emily Stone <emily.stone@novushealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 May 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: environment selection and audit evidence scoping

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on hosting modality and the evidence Novus will need for your HIPAA pipeline.

Summary of options we discussed (tradeoffs at a glance):
- Hosted API: fastest onboarding, shared infra, Redwood retains SOC2 controls and can sign a BAA; best for early product validation but requires tight data minimization and strict routing.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for your workloads (single-tenant compute), data isolation at the runtime layer, faster time-to-prod than full private deployment; recommended if you want predictable throughput with fewer network integrations.
- Private VPC / On-prem: customer-controlled networking, optional on-prem package for air-gapped needs, supports customer-managed KMS/HSM and stricter audit controls — the highest compliance surface but longer lead time.

Compliance evidence checklist (what Novus asked for today):
- Latest SOC2 Type II report summary and scope
- Executable BAA draft and signature cadence
- Encryption at-rest and in-transit details (algorithms, KMS model)
- Audit log availability (token-level, API-level), retention windows, and export process
- Network connectivity options for Private (VPN, Direct Connect) and sample firewall rules
- Pen test / vulnerability assessment summary and remediation SLAs

Action items / next steps:
1) I’ll attach the Redwood evidence asklist and a high-level architecture diagram for Private vs Dedicated so your security team can mark must-haves. (attached)
2) Can you share the internal security requirements spreadsheet and preferred timeline for evidence review?
3) If Novus wants a Private deployment, we’ll set up an architecture deep-dive and a PKI/KMS integration call with infra (typically 2–3 weeks to scope). If Dedicated is acceptable initially, we can onboard in 1–2 weeks after contract.

Proposed meeting: Wed May 10, 10:00 AM PT for a 30–45 min compliance deep-dive. I’ll wait for confirm.

Thanks —
Alex Martinez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0147

From: Emily Stone <emily.stone@novushealth.com>

Cc: NovusHealth Security Team <security@novushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 07 May 2028 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: environment selection and audit evidence scoping

Alex — thanks for the clear recap. I ran the summary by our security lead and a couple quick clarifications before we lock the next steps:

1) Private VPC vs on-prem: our preference is Private VPC with the option to move to on-prem later. Key ask: does Redwood support customer-managed HSM (BYOK) in the Private model, or is HSM only available on-prem?
2) BAA: we need confirmation that Redwood will sign a standard BAA and whether you have an editable draft today.
3) SOC2: can you provide the most recent SOC2 Type II report and an estimate for how long it will take you to produce any specific supplementary evidence (e.g., retention configuration snapshots, audit log exports) after request?
4) Network: if we choose Private we will need a VPN/DX option and example firewall templates to pass to our network team.

I attached our security_requirements.xlsx — it has items your team can tick off to speed the review. Our target is to complete evidence review within 30 business days if feasible. Also please call out any items that would require an on-prem deployment or additional procurement.

Thanks —
Emily Stone
Director, Product Security | NovusHealth
emily.stone@novushealth.com
Attachments: security_requirements.xlsx (xlsx)

Hi Emily —

Following up from Alex’s recap with a bit more detail from our compliance and infra side. Short answers to your questions:

- BYOK / HSM: Private deployments support customer-managed keys via a bring-your-own-key model integrating with cloud KMS (AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault). For dedicated HSM appliances (FIPS 140-2 level), we offer an on-prem option or can integrate with a customer-managed HSM in your cloud account depending on the provider. We’ll need to scope connectivity and key provisioning in the architecture review.

- BAA: Redwood will sign a BAA for HIPAA-covered use cases. I’m attaching a redlined BAA draft and a short SOC2 summary that lists the scope controls.

- SOC2 & evidence turnaround: We maintain a rolling SOC2 Type II audit; the latest completed report is for period ending Dec 31, 2027. For ad-hoc evidence (log extracts, retention configuration), typical turnaround is 5–15 business days depending on the level of detail requested. For anything that requires change (e.g., longer retention or custom logging hooks) we’ll need an onboarding sprint (2–4 weeks).

Recommended path for Novus based on call:
1) Short term: provision Dedicated capacity so you can start ingestion and iterate on prompts while we run the Private design in parallel.
2) Parallel: schedule architecture & PKI call (technical deep-dive) to scope VPN/DX and HSM integration — we’ll bring infra and product security.
3) Legal: get the BAA draft exchanged and routed for signatures concurrently.

I’ve attached: soc2-summary.pdf, pki-integration-guide.docx, and a BAA draft to the legal thread (we’ll send DocuSign link on request).

If this sounds right I’ll lock the Wed May 10 slot that Alex proposed.

—Laura
